correctness.rationale: The existence and diameter claims hold for every fixed f≥4 and δ>0. The geometry can be checked directly from RESULT.md §1: choose R>4 large enough that arcsin(4/R)<δ. The projected initial three normals surround zero strictly (each successive angular gap, including the wraparound gap, is <π). With their positive vertical coordinates and the downward base normal they positively span in 3D. The three side planes at offset 1 and the base z=0 bound a full-dimensional tetrahedron. The normal recurrence follows from roots R and exp(±iθ); its positive coefficients express the new normal in the interior of the normal cone at the current top vertex. A sufficiently shallow cut removes just that vertex, creates a triangle, and preserves simplicity. Side facet neighbors have index difference at most three by induction. Their horizontal dot products for differences 1, 2, 3 are −1/R, 2/R²−1, 3/R−4/R³, respectively; the vertical contribution is ≤1/R², so the normalized dot products are <4/R, and base-side dihedrals are acute. For the graph, at k≥5 the new vertices U_k,W_k,T_k link to W_(k−1),U_(k−2),U_(k−1), respectively, with H differences 3; the replacement triangle has differences 1,1,2. The base tetrahedron and the two exceptional steps k=3,4 obey the same bound by direct substitution. Consequently the specified endpoints are at distance at least ceil((2k−1)/3). Every intermediate distance layer separating endpoints has at least three vertices by 3-connectivity. Euler and minimum degree three yield V≤2f−4 also for nonsimple polytopes, giving the matching universal upper bound.
